intro: Three of the four numbers (or pairs) follow the same rule, and one doesn't. Find the rule the three share; the one left over is the answer.

tips.title: Find what three have in common
tips.body: Look for a rule that three of them share: all prime, all squares, all divisible by 11, digits that add up to the same total…

tips.title: Look inside the digits
tips.body: Many questions use the digits: the middle digit is the sum or product of the outer two, or all the digits add up to the same total.

tips.title: Pairs? Find the link
tips.body: For pairs like 5, 50 and 11, 242, work out how the second number comes from the first (here 2 × n²), then test each pair.

tips.title: Know the special numbers
tips.body: Learn the primes up to 100, the squares up to 20² and the cubes up to 10³. They give the most common rules.

tips.title: Don't stop at odd or even
tips.body: If one number is just odd or even, look for a deeper rule as well. The question usually means the deeper rule.
